title: The strait and narrow: Yemen, the Red Sea and Europe’s path forward – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: ECFR policy alert: the Houthis have seized the Red Sea coast needed to command Bab al-Mandab, the route Saudi crude now depends on after Iran closed Hormuz, while Iraqi militias hit Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline; Riyadh has cancelled crude exports to Europe. The authors urge more EU naval support (Atalanta, Aspides) for Riyadh but warn military action in Yemen will fail and push a middle-power coalition to end the US-Iran war.

insights.claim: Since Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz forced Saudi Arabia to reroute crude through the Red Sea, the Houthis have seized the coastal stretch needed to command the Bab al-Mandab strait.
insights.speaker: Julien Barnes-Dacey, Cinzia Bianco, Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Both main Gulf crude chokepoints are now contested, a major oil supply risk.
insights.quote: They recently seized the stretch needed to command the Bab al-Mandab, the strait that Saudi crude must pass through to reach open water since Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz

insights.claim: Iraqi militias have attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which carries 90% of current Saudi exports via the Red Sea.
insights.speaker: Julien Barnes-Dacey, Cinzia Bianco, Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Saudi export capacity's single point of failure is under attack.
insights.quote: Iraqi militias have also attacked the kingdom’s East-West pipeline, which carries 90% of current Saudi exports via the Red Sea

insights.claim: The Suez Canal remains open but is not a real alternative for the large tankers Saudi Arabia needs to reach Asia and Europe.
insights.speaker: Julien Barnes-Dacey, Cinzia Bianco, Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Tanker size constraints limit rerouting; supports elevated freight rates and crude premiums.

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia has cancelled crude exports to Europe, where the US-Iran war is already causing energy shortages, higher prices and a deepening cost-of-living crisis.
insights.speaker: Julien Barnes-Dacey, Cinzia Bianco, Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Bullish European crude/product prices and bearish European consumer demand.

insights.claim: Riyadh has begun strikes in Yemen and is seeking allies for a wider campaign, with the US weighing involvement in exchange for deeper Saudi support against Iran.
insights.speaker: Julien Barnes-Dacey, Cinzia Bianco, Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Risk of regional war widening into a Saudi-Houthi front.

insights.claim: The Houthis largely refrained from attacks after US strikes on Iran began in February, but that restraint is ending likely because Iran, under US pressure, is mobilising allies to widen the conflict's cost.
insights.speaker: Julien Barnes-Dacey, Cinzia Bianco, Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Iran's proxy escalation strategy suggests more attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure.
insights.quote: However, this restraint is now ending likely because Iran, under growing US pressure, is trying to mobilise allies to widen the cost of the regional conflict.
insights.locator: After US strikes on Iran began

insights.claim: Military action in Yemen will not solve the conflict: a decade of similar campaigns has failed, the Houthis can disrupt waterways via low-cost warfare, and intra-GCC rivalries keep the anti-Houthi camp divided.
insights.speaker: Julien Barnes-Dacey, Cinzia Bianco, Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Do not price a quick military reopening of Bab al-Mandab.
insights.quote: Military action in Yemen will not solve the conflict, as a decade of similar campaigns has already failed.
insights.locator: Military action in Yemen will not

insights.claim: Europe should rapidly increase resources for EUNAVFOR Atalanta and Aspides, adding minesweeping and counter-drone cover, and deepen cooperation with the Saudi-led Multinational Maritime Defence Alliance ahead of October's EU-GCC summit.
insights.speaker: Julien Barnes-Dacey, Cinzia Bianco, Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Demand for naval minesweeping and counter-drone capabilities in Europe.

insights.claim: Because the US-Iran conflict is now directly interlinked with Yemen's, Europe should lead a middle-power coalition including Middle Eastern states, Pakistan and Canada to press Washington and Tehran back to diplomacy, using the UN General Assembly.
insights.speaker: Julien Barnes-Dacey, Cinzia Bianco, Ellie Geranmayeh
insights.so_what: Diplomatic de-escalation push is the main path to reopening chokepoints.

source_meta.author: Julien Barnes-Dacey, Cinzia Bianco, Ellie Geranmayeh
